title: ElastiCache: choose managed cache and queue roles deliberately
outcome: Separate cache data from durable work and plan client behavior during eviction or failover.
useCase: Rails caches, sessions, and queue infrastructure.
drawbacks: Role mixing and fallback behavior can threaten correctness or the DB.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: Same protocol does not mean the same data responsibility.

trace.title: Choose data role
trace.detail: ElastiCache supplies managed in-memory engines/options. Identify the selected engine and mode rather than assuming every Redis-compatible feature and durability behavior is identical. Client compatibility, topology, authentication, TLS, and failover matter.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Cache miss → authoritative DB read → cached copy → later hit → expiry/eviction → rebuild. Then trace failover: client connection breaks, DNS/topology changes, operations retry under the selected contract.

Monitor memory, eviction, latency, connection count, and application fallback load. A cache outage can overload PostgreSQL if every request immediately falls back.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A cache is not permission authority. A Redis queue on an eviction-enabled shared cache can lose work. A cold-cache stampede can create a database incident.
